newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says easing NZ monetary policy no answer.
newsitem.headline: Peters says easing NZ monetary policy no answer.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters told a New Zealand investment conference on Tuesday that the government was well aware of pressure faced by exporters from the appreciating exchange rate, but he said loosening monetary policy was not the answer.

"Looser monetary policy is not the answer to relieving this pressure. Any temporary relief would soon be eroded by rising costs," he said, adding there was general agreement on that across the political divide.
Peters said that while there would be increased government spending, the government would spend wisely, not for the sake of it.
Reducing debt was a priority so that the government was in a strong position to withstand changes in economic conditions without having to make abrupt changes in taxes or expenses, he said.
"Lower debt reduces real interest rates throughout the economy by reducing the risk premium on capital."
He said the long term goal, if macro-economic conditions deemed it wise, was to eliminate debt.
"Maintaining fiscal surpluses will enable further debt reduction and boost national savings."
Peters said that what distinguished the new centre-right coalition government from the previous conservative National Party government was the prominence given to the value of self reliance.
New Zealand had to be outward looking, he said.
The key to maintaining international competitiveness was: stable economic policies; deregulated, competitive and open markets; quality public services; and lowest possible tax rates, Peters said.
